cultural.vision_reason: A carved alder-wood grease bowl in raven form, executed in classic Haida formline style, is a traditional Haida feast/ceremonial vessel type.

physical.title: bowl
physical.summary: Bowl, for grease, of alder wood, in the form of a raven, the bowl/body of oval form, with 3-dimensional head, tail and hawk's heads on the tail and chest. The raven head is carved in classic Haida style, with over the ears a human mask facing towards the bowl. Under the chin is a break or broken addition, fixed with a metal pin, and on the chest a large hawk's head; the sides of the bowl are carved with low relief wings, also carved in 3-dimensions at the back alongside the tail, which is also carved with a hawk's head. The bird's claws are carved in low relief under the tail. The mask on the raven's head has human arms, carved in low relief down the rim of the bowl. The interior of the bowl has been carved out to leave thin walls, and a sharp lip on the inside of the bowl.
